drhp.business: Hi-Green Carbon Limited is engaged in the manufacturing and trading of hydrocarbon fuel by recycling waste rubber, along with various other allied products. Through continuous pyrolysis technology, the Company processes end-of-life tyres to produce TPO, rCB, Syngas and steel scrap, and during the year it added a Renewable Technology Solutions business, broadening its capabilities beyond tyre recycling.
drhp.expansion: Hi-Green's manufacturing footprint expanded significantly during the year with the commissioning of additional facilities; together with its subsidiaries, the Company reached an aggregate tyre pyrolysis capacity of 300 TPD through three plants of 100 TPD each. The commencement of operations at the Madhya Pradesh facility further strengthened its presence and opened opportunities for value addition through utilisation of Syngas and other by-products. During the year the Company also added a Renewable Technology Solutions business, broadening its capabilities beyond tyre recycling.
drhp.mdna: Revenue from Operations grew on continued expansion of business operations and sustained demand for the Company's products.|Manufacturing footprint expanded with commissioning of additional facilities, strengthening raw material sourcing, customer reach and operational efficiency.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthening position in the circular economy and sustainable materials space by expanding processing capabilities and deepening technological strengths.
- Maximising value from waste tyres through continuous pyrolysis technology, producing TPO, rCB, Syngas and steel scrap, while exploring further downstream applications.
- Broadening capabilities beyond tyre recycling into Renewable Technology Solutions by leveraging the Group's experience in renewable energy and sustainable technologies.
- Focus on operational efficiency, product quality, cost optimisation, compliance and strengthening customer relationships in response to commodity and crude-oil price volatility and geopolitical developments.
